About

As large language models and AI agents take on requirements, coding, testing, and repair, the roles humans play in software engineering keep evolving.

NEXUS 2027 brings together researchers, students, and practitioners from software engineering, AI, HCI, and related areas to discuss what humans uniquely contribute, how human–AI and human–human relationships are changing, and where human roles are heading.

A presentation-centered workshop. Submissions are reviewed primarily on a recorded presentation rather than a written paper.

Call for Submissions

We welcome original research, new ideas and perspectives, and industry experience reports on human roles in software engineering. Previously published work is also welcome.

Topics include, but are not limited to

  • Human factors in requirements engineering, software design, development, testing, and maintenance
  • Human knowledge, expertise, judgment, and creativity in software engineering, and their value
  • Human–AI interaction and collaboration, including the division of labor between developers and AI agents
  • Human oversight, validation, and trust in AI-generated artifacts and autonomous software engineering agents
  • Socio-technical aspects of communication and collaboration among developers, users, and other stakeholders
  • Developer experience, productivity, skills, cognition, and well-being in AI-assisted software development
  • Software engineering education and the evolving roles of software engineers

How to Submit

Required

Recorded presentation

Up to 20 minutes, self-contained. No professional production needed.

  • MP4 (H.264)
  • ≤ 1080p
  • ≤ 600 MB
  • + slides (PDF)
Optional

Extended abstract

Up to 4 pages, excluding references.

Optional

Supplementary materials

Manuscript, data, code, or replication package.

Review criteria

Each submission receives at least three reviews, considering both research quality and presentation quality.

  1. RelevanceContributes to understanding human roles in software engineering.
  2. OriginalityClearly communicates its contributions and novelty.
  3. SoundnessIs sound and supported by appropriate evidence.
  4. ClarityClearly communicates the essential content of the research.
  5. SignificanceHas implications for software engineering research or practice.
  • Authors may choose either single-blind or double-blind review.
  • Submissions of previously published work must clearly identify the original publication.
  • Submissions will be managed through HotCRP. The submission link will be posted here when submissions open.

After Acceptance

Optional journal path

Accepted unpublished work is pre-registered for publication as a full paper in Software Engineering Nexus, subject to the journal's review and revision.
